capability_investigated:
WhisperProcessor feature extractor framing (fixed 30s mel window) and the
batch interface of frozen.asr_backend.generate — it accepts an (N, n_mels,
n_frames) StorageView with a list of N prompts and returns N results.
what_i_learned:
The extractor pads/truncates any input to exactly one 30s window, so the
stub silently dropped everything after 0:30 of each call (structural
deletion, length_ratio floored). generate() is batched over the leading
axis, so multiple 30s windows can be decoded in one call and concatenated.
hypothesis:
Split the waveform into consecutive non-overlapping 30s windows, extract mel
features per window, decode them all in one batched generate() call, and join
the per-window text in order. This recovers the deleted tail — the dominant
error axis for multi-minute 0715 calls — without touching decode params.

capability_investigated:
GPU memory behavior of frozen.asr_backend.generate when fed an
(N, n_mels, n_frames) batch — the OOM crash from iter_001's all-windows-in-
one-call batch on multi-minute 0715 calls.
what_i_learned:
The batched generate() over the leading axis allocates decode state for all
N windows at once on a float16 CUDA model; long calls (many 30s windows)
exceed GPU memory and raise "CUDA failed with error out of memory". Peak
memory scales with batch size, so decoding windows sequentially (batch=1)
keeps the structural-deletion fix while staying within VRAM.
hypothesis:
Keep the 30s windowing that recovers the truncated tail, but iterate windows
one at a time through generate() and concatenate the per-window text. This
removes the OOM crash while preserving the length-ratio recovery.

capability_investigated:
generate()'s **decoding_kwargs surface — specifically the beam-search and
anti-repetition knobs the frozen docstring advertises (beam_size, patience,
repetition_penalty) plus no_repeat_ngram_size, none of which the parent
pipeline uses (it decodes pure-greedy beam_size=1, temp=0.0).
what_i_learned:
The parent's per-window deletion is not purely structural windowing loss:
4/12 files carry the repeated_text flag (repeated 0.27) while length_ratio
sits at 0.65. That is the classic greedy long-form Whisper failure — the
decoder enters a repetition loop, spends the per-window token budget on a
repeated run, and the collapsed run reads as deletion. So the repetition
axis and the coverage axis share one cause, addressable purely through
decode params with no new mechanism.
hypothesis:
Replace greedy decode with beam_size=5 + patience=1.0 to stop premature
collapse, and add repetition_penalty=1.15 + no_repeat_ngram_size=3 to break
loops before they consume the budget. This should raise length_ratio and
cut the repeated_text rate, lowering corpus_cer. Cost ~5x inference
(105s parent → ~525s) stays under the 719.9s budget.

capability_investigated:
The prompt-token side of generate()'s decode path — specifically the
<|notimestamps|> special token that every prior iteration pinned in the
forced prompt, and the alternative timestamp-decoding regime that omitting it
unlocks (the decoder then emits <|t|> segment-boundary tokens in the returned
sequences_ids). Never used in the ledger, which only covered mel framing,
batched-OOM, and beam/repetition decode kwargs.
what_i_learned:
Coverage loss is not just blind 30s cutting — in <|notimestamps|> greedy mode
large-v3 emits EOT early within a window on dense multi-utterance audio,
transcribing only the front and stopping, which is exactly the length_ratio
0.65 / deletion-80% signature. The frozen surface lets me switch to the
trained timestamp regime purely by dropping <|notimestamps|> from the forced
prompt; the returned sequences_ids then carry timestamp tokens (every id >=
<|0.00|>) which I filter out before tokenizer.decode so they don't pollute
text. Stride stays fixed 30s, so decode-call count and runtime are unchanged.
hypothesis:
Decoding each 30s window in timestamp mode (prompt without <|notimestamps|>)
keeps the model transcribing to the window end instead of terminating early,
raising length_ratio and cutting the dominant deletion axis without adding
windows or risking the runtime budget. Timestamp tokens are stripped from
sequences_ids before text decode.

capability_investigated:
The numeric value of the timestamp tokens in generate()'s returned
sequences_ids — not their presence (family_003 already established that
dropping <|notimestamps|> makes them appear), but that each id decodes to a
wall-clock offset via (id - timestamp_begin) * 0.02, letting me locate where
each emitted segment sits inside the 30s window.
what_i_learned:
family_003's hallucination regression (0.091 -> 0.182) rides on the feature
extractor's silent padding of the final short window: in timestamp mode
large-v3 keeps emitting <|t|> segments past the real audio and invents text
for the padding. The timestamp values family_003 discarded are exactly the
signal to gate that — a segment whose start offset >= len(chunk)/sr is
padding-region and can be dropped, with full 30s windows unaffected.
hypothesis:
Keep timestamp decoding (family_003 coverage) but parse segment boundaries
and keep only text whose segment starts before real_seconds = len(chunk)/sr,
composing family_003's length_ratio win with family_001's lower hallucination
instead of trading one for the other.
